brand_fidelity.evidence: Every colour comes from the palette. Signal appears only on the primary buttons and the 24×3px wordmark rule. Negatives use a true minus sign in Harbour, positives use Kelp, and the error message uses Harbour with a Harbour left rule instead of red. Fraunces 600 and Plex 400/500 load correctly, sizes stay on the 14/16/20/28/40 scale, money has tabular-nums, radius is 6px, there are no shadows, and focus uses a 2px Harbour outline with 2px offset.

visual_craft.evidence: Hierarchy is clear: a 40px wordmark, 28px Fraunces section heads, a 20px 'Settle up' sub-head, and Fog metadata. Spacing rhythm is consistent and the two-column description/amount grid collapses cleanly on mobile. At 390px the expense meta line wraps to three cramped lines because the amount and the Remove button take so much row width. Settle up sits flush under the balances with no extra separation.

copy_voice.evidence: Errors say what to fix: 'Enter an amount with at most 2 decimal places.', 'Ana is already on the trip. Enter a different name.' Empty states are single next-step sentences, and the empty expense list adapts its wording to whether people exist yet. Buttons are 'Add person', 'Add expense', 'Remove', and the balance labels 'is owed / owes / is even' are calm and plain.

ux_completeness.evidence: All required flows work: case-insensitive duplicate check, inline errors that keep typed values and focus the offending field, and a newest-first expense list with payer and split names. Removing an expense moves focus sensibly, balances show with labels, and the greedy settle-up is readable as 'Ben pays Ana'. Checkbox state is preserved across re-renders. Gaps are small: people can't be removed, and the mobile expense rows are dense.

code_quality.evidence: Integer-cents parsing avoids floats, remainder cents go out in trip order, and the greedy debtor/creditor matching guarantees at most n−1 transfers. Markup is semantic (forms, fieldset/legend, labelled inputs, aria-live, a descriptive aria-label on Remove). Weaker points: minified one-line CSS and JS, inline style attributes generated in JS, and aria-invalid cleared only on some fields after a successful submit.

directed_design.evidence: Restrained and specific to the brief. The error style avoids red, people are shown as quiet rectangular chips, and balance rows pair the amount with a small status word. It still follows a fairly standard three-panel stacked-card layout with no distinctive touches beyond following the guidelines closely.

ai_tells: Inline style attributes injected from JS (style:'font-weight:500', style:'display:block;text-align:right;font-weight:500') instead of classes.
review.best_detail: Negative balances use a typographic minus in Harbour with a small Fog 'owes' label, and validation errors use a Harbour left-rule rather than red, honouring 'owing is normal, not an error' exactly.
review.worst_detail: On mobile the expense row keeps the amount and Remove button inline, squeezing 'Paid by Chloe · Split between Ana, Ben, Chloe' into a narrow three-line column.
